title: Add an option to show facets anyway if there is no results
body:
You can see the behavior here.

https://magento.algolia.com/catalogsearch/result/?q=__empty__#q=dd&page=0&refinements=%5B%7B%22color%22%3A%5B%22Purple%22%5D%7D%2C%7B%22categories%22%3A%5B%22Sale%22%5D%7D%5D&numerics_refinements=%7B%7D&index_name=%22magento_default_products%22

comments.body: How do you do it in magento?

For now I have no nice way to handle that.

So :
- I created a second helper that just do an empty query if no results are found in the first helper
- Re-display only the facet block and adding a empty class on each facet refinements
- When I click on a facet if an empty class is here, I set the query to ""

That's why I ask for algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js#146 to avoid this double helper.

> I created a second helper that just do an empty query if no results are found in the first helper

The other option would be to always keep the last state and avoid replacing the facets block if there are no results. Isn't it?
No I don't think so because we want the count for an empty query with the current refinements, which is not always the last state

> That's why I ask for algolia/algoliasearch-helper-js#146 to avoid this double helper.

Now I better understand your usecase in the helper. Would have been good to start with the real use case instead of the API need :dancer: :D

> The other option would be to always keep the last state and avoid replacing the facets block if there are no results. Isn't it?

"last state" seems too broad to me. Do you mean the last helper state or an inner state of the widget. I'm not even sure this would fix the issue.

> "last state" seems too broad to me. Do you mean the last helper state or an inner state of the widget. I'm not even sure this would fix the issue.

The helper state should be enough to display any widget (Famous last words)

> "last state" seems too broad to me. Do you mean the last helper state or an inner state of the widget. I'm not even sure this would fix the issue.

I mean, the last state returning results :)
Still unsure if this is a good practice or not, the "last state returning results" being not so easy to grasp for a user. I do prefer the simple "start over" or "hit back" method.

`currentRefinedValues` (#404) will solve part of the problem, so I think we shouldn't think about it for the v1, but it might make sense to implement this on faceting widgets, let's wait until we see if there is a demand for this.
